drafts.window: ~11 AM MT Saturday (Sat heatmap: midnight–1 AM; 5–7 AM; ~11 AM). Soft-pedal weekday 11–2 as primary for Saturday.
drafts.angle: CarsDirect updated Sep 19: 2026 Uncharted Premium FWD lease about $405/mo for 36 months with only $1,415 due (effective ~$444 before tax). Also 0% APR + cash combo paths. Kitchen-table: low drive-off is the story, not the brochure monthly alone. Soft-pedal Fri EV6/Niro twins if those Chrome drafts are still unposted.
bullets: CarsDirect (updated Sep 19, 2026): 2026 Uncharted Premium FWD ~$405/mo, 36 mo, $1,415 due; effective ~$444/mo before taxes and fees; expires ~Sep 30, 2026.
MSRP on that Premium FWD line ~$36,445 (CarsDirect).
Electrek manufacturer table (~Sep 13): Uncharted Prem FWD ~$405 / avg monthly cost ~$433 with ~$1,415 due.

drafts.body:
Most EV lease ads scream the monthly and hide the drive-off. Uncharted flips that.

CarsDirect still shows a 2026 Premium FWD around $405 a month for 36 months with about $1,415 due. Once you average the drive-off, you are nearer $440 a month before tax. That is a different kitchen-table conversation than a $369 sticker with $4,000 due.

US kitchen-table take for a 42-year-old shopping a compact EV crossover, or a 60-year-old who wants a simple payment stack:

1) Ask for the out-the-door sheet on the exact Premium VIN, not a website monthly.
2) Divide the $1,415 by 36, then add the payment. That is your real lease number.
3) Quote insurance on that VIN before you sign.
4) Map weekday Level 2 at home, work, or a real apartment plan if you rent.

35-54 line: Premium timelines save low drive-off math. This is a save-and-repost payment post.

55+ line: a small due-at-signing only helps if insurance and the plug plan keep your independence.

drafts.angle: Canary / CT Mirror Sep 18: $6.2B Revolution Wind installed final of 65 turbines; 704 MW full capacity later this year; already partial power to RI and CT since March. Winter storm + July heat wave: offshore wind cut oil peaker reliance. Kitchen-table: more local generation = less "who pays for peak" surprise. Soft-pedal politics sermon. Soft-pedal UK NAO wires twin. He RTed the headline; this draft is original household bill frame, not an RT twin.
bullets: Canary Media (Sep 18, 2026): Revolution Wind installed its 65th and final turbine; $6.2 billion project; up to 704 MW full capacity "later this year"; partial output to Rhode Island and Connecticut since March.
Same piece: Vineyard Wind 1 and Revolution Wind helped New England lean less on oil-burning peakers during the July heat wave; Vineyard Wind 1 and South Fork also showed up in Winter Storm Fern.
Also complete at scale: South Fork (NY) and Vineyard Wind 1 (MA). Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind (~2.6 GW) delivering since March; Empire Wind and Sunrise Wind eyed for 2027.
Soft-pedal stop-work politics as the hook; keep "bill certainty / less peaker oil" as the hook.
Soft-pedal UK NAO constraint-cost twin and standing UK wires posts.
drafts.body:
Wind is not a slogan when your July bill spikes because the grid leans on oil peakers.

Revolution Wind just finished standing its 65th turbine off Rhode Island. The project is a $6.2 billion build that can deliver up to 704 megawatts once it is fully online later this year. Rhode Island and Connecticut have already been taking partial power since March.

The kitchen-table part: when New England hit a nasty winter storm and a brutal July heat wave, offshore wind helped utilities burn less expensive oil for peak. That is reliability money, not a climate sermon.

US household take (even if you live in Colorado):

1) Screenshot your delivery and generation lines on a peak-month bill.
2) Ask your utility or co-op what "peaker" fuel shows up on extreme days.
3) If you are in New England, ask how Revolution / Vineyard / South Fork show up in your rate case language.
4) Save tools that explain residential rates in your ZIP. Certainty is the product.

35-54 line: Premium timelines share "who pays for peak" stories.

55+ line: fixed-income homes feel peaker spikes first. Ask what is on the margin.

drafts.window: ~11 AM MT Saturday (Sat heatmap: midnight–1 AM; 5–7 AM; ~11 AM). Soft-pedal weekday 11–2 as primary for Saturday.
drafts.angle: Cool Down / ILSR tracker: NY added 202 MW community solar in Q2 2026 (~7% growth); only NJ, NY, Oregon topped 1% QoQ for three straight quarters; only 18 states + DC allow community solar; ~91% of capacity in 10 states. Kitchen-table: bill credits without a roof. Soft-pedal NJ ≥15% Wed pack twin; soft-pedal balcony/CA plug-in standing.
bullets: The Cool Down (Sep 17, 2026) citing ILSR Community Solar Tracker / PV Magazine: New York added 202 MW of community solar capacity in Q2 2026 (~7% growth) and was the only state to accelerate vs Q1.
Only New Jersey, New York, and Oregon topped 1% quarter-over-quarter capacity growth for three straight quarters.
Only 18 states plus Washington, D.C. allow community solar; NREL figures via coverage: ~91% of U.S. community solar capacity sits in just 10 states.
NYSERDA: homeowners, renters, businesses, and multifamily can subscribe and receive bill credits without panels on their roof.
Soft-pedal Wed NJ community solar ≥15% twin; soft-pedal CA balcony / plug-in bills pending signature.
drafts.body:
If you rent, or your roof is shaded, "solar is not for me" is often outdated.

Community solar is a shared project that puts bill credits on your utility statement. New York just added about 202 megawatts of that capacity in a single quarter. That is real scale. It is also a reminder that the map is uneven: only about 18 states plus D.C. even allow these programs.

US kitchen-table take:

1) Google your state + "community solar" + your utility name.
2) Compare at least two offers on estimated bill credit percent, contract length, and early-exit fees.
3) If your state is not on the list of 18, ask your PUC why renters are locked out.
4) Homeowners with good roofs: still run a rooftop quote in parallel. Do not assume community is always cheaper.

35-54 line: renter solar access is a Premium reply magnet.

55+ line: bill credits without climbing a roof is independence for older households.

drafts.title: Cox Aug new-EV ATP $54,754 / premium ~$4,847
drafts.window: ~11 AM MT Saturday (Sat heatmap: midnight–1 AM; 5–7 AM; ~11 AM). Soft-pedal weekday 11–2 as primary for Saturday.
drafts.angle: Cox Automotive Aug 2026 (Electric Cars Report / KBB): new EV ATP $54,754 (down 1.3% MoM); premium over ICE+ narrowed to $4,847 (~9.7%); incentives ~$6,594 avg (~12% of ATP). Used EV avg listing $37,441; used days' supply 42 (parity with ICE+). Soft-pedal Fri used days-to-sell Recurrent twin and Tue +5.1% price-firming twin. Kitchen-table: the premium is shrinking.
bullets: Electric Cars Report summarizing Cox Automotive Aug 2026: new EV average transaction price $54,754 (down 1.3% MoM, down 2.8% YoY).
EV premium over ICE+ narrowed to $4,847 (~9.7%); average incentives ~$6,594 (~12% of ATP).
Used EV average listing price $37,441 (down 1% MoM, up 8.2% YoY); used EV days' supply fell to 42 (parity with ICE+ for first time in 2026).
Used EV sales ~44,350 in August (+25.9% MoM, +14.7% YoY). New EV sales ~78,895 (+2.5% MoM).
Soft-pedal Fri AP8 Recurrent "Bolt sells in 12 days" twin and Tue used +5.1% firming twin.
drafts.body:
People still argue about EVs like it is 2022 sticker shock. The average gap is not that story anymore.

In August, the average new EV transaction price landed around $54,754. The premium over a comparable gas vehicle narrowed to about $4,847. That is under 10%. Incentives still average roughly $6,600, so the out-the-door fight is real, but the "EVs are automatically $15k more" talking point is getting stale.

Used side: average listing around $37,441, and used EV inventory days matched gas at about 42 days. Demand is absorbing the lease-return wave instead of flooding lots.

US kitchen-table take:

1) Compare out-the-door on the exact EV VIN vs the gas trim you would actually buy.
2) Add 5-year fuel + maintenance in your ZIP (not a national meme).
3) Quote insurance on both VINs before you decide.
4) If new still feels rich, shop 2-4 year used with a battery health report.

35-54 line: "$4,800 premium" is a Premium timeline number.

55+ line: independence is the payment you can sleep on, new or used.
